messages.content: "1255 :     public StrBuilder appendFixedWidthPadRight(int value, int width, char padChar) {\n1256 :         return appendFixedWidthPadRight(String.valueOf(value), width, padChar);\n1257 :     }"

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The issue relates to the method StrBuilder.appendFixedWidthPadRight(Object, int, char) which is invoked by the failing test with a null input. Inspecting the method implementation reveals that if the width parameter is greater than zero, it tries to convert the provided object to a String using:
```java
String str = (obj == null ? getNullText() : obj.toString());
```
If the object is null, it calls getNullText() to obtain the string to append. However, from the StrBuilder.getNullText() implementation, we see it simply returns the private variable nullText, which appears to be uninitialized or null by default (since the constructor does not seem to set it).

As a result, if null is passed and nullText has not been set, getNullText() returns null, assigning null to str. Subsequent calls such as str.length() will cause a NullPointerException.

The test failed because sb.appendFixedWidthPadRight(null, 10, '*') passes null, triggering this code path. Since no null text is defined, this leads to a null pointer error.

Hence the root cause of the bug is that appendFixedWidthPadRight does not handle the case where the null text is null, leading to an exception instead of gracefully handling or substituting a default string for nulls.

No relevant information was found in recent bug reports that would affect this diagnosis.

The fix should ensure that getNullText() never returns null or appendFixedWidthPadRight handles null returns properly by substituting a default string like "" or "null". 

This explains the failure in the test and the null pointer exception described in the bug report.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
